Its working range runs from an octave below middle C to two octaves above middle C; a B footjoint lowers it by one more semitone. Its dynamic range is gentle, and in a large ensemble it is easily masked, so the balance has to be managed by light scoring or amplification. The low register works best in solo playing, small ensembles and flute choirs; a C footjoint makes the instrument shorter, quicker to respond and brighter. High notes in the written range are not always stable and can be corrected with the embouchure or alternative fingerings.

In 1910 Abelardo Albisi invented a bass flute called the albisiphone, used in works by Mascagni and Zandonai and others. In the early twentieth century English composers used 'bass flute' for the alto flute: Holst's The Planets marks a bass flute in G, and the usage appears in several works by Britten. New variants appeared in the 1920s and opened up the low register of the ductless woodwind in jazz. From 1975 Jeremy Steig used one on the album Temple of Birth; the bass flute in F is really a contrabass flute. It is not widely used today and is more often found in flute choirs; in a wind band it is easily covered by the clarinets.

The bass flute belongs to the flute family of aerophones, Hornbostel–Sachs 421.121.12, and sounds an octave below the standard flute. Its tube is about 146 centimetres long, twice that of the standard flute, and it has a J-shaped headjoint that brings the embouchure hole within reach. The player controls pitch with the embouchure and uses the keys and the trill key to steady the middle register. It is common in flute choirs, small ensembles and solo playing; in a large ensemble its timbre is easily covered and needs light scoring or amplification. Jazz players and film and game scores have also used it.
演奏時需以口型對準吹孔，因管身較長，頭節採J形以便吹孔可及。初學先練習持穩樂器，: The embouchure has to be aimed at the embouchure hole, and because the tube is long the headjoint is J-shaped so that the hole can be reached. A beginner first practises holding the instrument steady, using a seat support rod, a thumb rest or an upright design to take the weight if needed. Sound comes from the air crossing the embouchure hole; when high notes run sharp the embouchure can correct them or an alternative fingering can be used, and unsteady notes in the middle register can be steadied with the trill key. The points to practise are balance, fingering, air and overblowing.
